studies.title: The effects of zinc supplementation on serum zinc and cholesterol concentrations in hemodialysis patients.
studies.abstract: To examine the effect of zinc sulfate supplementation on the concentrations of serum zinc and serum cholesterol in hemodialysis (HD) patients. Outpatient dialysis center in a large metropolitan city. Randomized, double-blind, before-after trial. Twenty-eight maintenance HD patients were selected. Twenty (15 women and 5 men) completed the study. Subjects were identified for inclusion in the study by the following criteria: HD treatment for a minimum of 6 months, no signs of gastrointestinal disorders, and no record of hospitalizations for reasons other than vascular access complications within the last 3 months. Patients were given a daily supplement of 7.7 micromol zinc sulfate (50 mg elemental zinc) or a cornstarch placebo capsule for 90 days. Patients completed 2-day food records, at day 0 and day 90 of the study, which included 1 dialysis day and 1 nondialysis day. Fasting, predialysis serum samples were collected on days 0, 40, and 90 to determine serum zinc and total cholesterol (TCHOL) concentrations. Dietary parameters, including zinc, protein, and energy intake, were also analyzed on days 0 and 90. Initial concentrations of serum zinc indicated subjects were below the normal range for serum zinc standards (12 micromol/L [80 microg/dL]). After supplementation, subjects in the zinc-supplemented group showed significant increases in serum zinc concentrations from 0.79 microg/mL at day 0 to 0.96 microg/mL at day 90. Serum TCHOL concentrations were initially low among subjects in the control (2.914 +/- 0.158 mmol/L [112.7 +/- 6.1 mg/dL]) and zinc-supplemented (3.155 +/- 0.354 mmol/L [122.0 +/- 13.7 mg/dL]) groups. Serum TCHOL concentrations in the control group increased slightly throughout the study period but did not reach statistical significance. A progressive increase in serum TCHOL concentration was observed in the zinc-supplemented group from the beginning (3.155 +/- 0.354 mmol/L [122.0 +/- 13.7 mg/dL]) to the end (4.445 +/- 0.478 mmol/L [171.9 +/- 18.5 mg/dL]) of the study (r =.63, P <.05). Mean serum high-density lipoprotein (HDL) cholesterol concentrations for the zinc-supplemented group were 0.959 mmol/L +/- 0.11 (37.1 mg/dL +/- 4.3), 0.825 mmol/L +/- 0.08 (31.9 mg/dL +/- 3.2), and 0.908 mmol/L +/- 0.10 (35.1 mg/dL +/- 3.9) from the beginning to the end of the experimental period. The mean serum HDL cholesterol concentrations for the control group were 0.760 mmol/L +/- 0.075 (29.4 mg/dL +/- 2.9), 0.760 +/- 0.08 (29.4 mg/dL +/- 3.0), and 0.799 mmol/L +/- 0.13 (30.9 mg/dL +/- 4.9) from the beginning to the end of the experimental period. A progressive increase in low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol concentration was observed for the zinc-supplemented group throughout the study. Mean LDL cholesterol concentrations for the zinc-supplemented group were 2.19 mmol/L +/- 0.39 (85 mg/dL +/- 15.0), 3.30 mmol/L +/- 0.36 (127.8 mg/dL +/- 14.1), and 3.53 mmol/L +/- 0.53 (136.7 mg/dL +/- 20.6) from the beginning to the end of the study peri

studies.title: Structural Elucidation and Zinc Supplement Potential of the High-Bioavailability Oyster Peptide-Zinc Complex.
studies.abstract: Zinc deficiency is a severe global public health problem. Traditional inorganic and organic zinc supplements have obvious drawbacks. Oysters are rich in zinc but suffer from insufficient deep processing and low economic value. Developing oyster peptide-zinc complex (OPZ) is a feasible solution for both zinc supplementation and high-value oyster utilization. This study optimized the chelation process of OPZ via single-factor and response surface methods. The optimal parameters were confirmed as follows: chelation time 44 min, temperature 50°C, pH 6.95, liquid-to-solid ratio 1:4, peptide-zinc ratio 1:1, with a chelation rate of 5.2498 mg/g. Multispectral characterization verified OPZ formation. Amino acids residues ─NH<sub>3</sub> <sup>+</sup> and ─COO<sup>-</sup> participated in chelation, and the peptide chain structure rearranged. OPZ showed good acid stability and gastrointestinal digestion resistance in simulated physiological conditions. In zinc-deficient mice, OPZ effectively restored body weight and food intake. It alleviated organ damage in liver, spleen, and small intestine. It also promoted zinc deposition in muscle, fur, serum, and femur to normal levels. OPZ had higher zinc bioavailability than zinc sulfate. This research clarifies OPZ's preparation and characterization. It provides technical support for oyster value-added processing. It also lays a foundation for developing efficient third-generation zinc supplements, with broad application prospects in functional foods and health products.

studies.title: Characterization of the gut microbiome and resistome of piglets supplemented with low, moderate, and high concentrations of zinc oxide.
studies.abstract:
The livestock sector is standing out for its substantial use of antimicrobials but is also investing in the development of mitigation strategies. Supranutritional concentrations of zinc (Zn) are served to piglets to prevent post-weaning diarrhea. This practice is detrimental to the piglet's assimilation of nutrients and can impact the environment through the excretion of unassimilated Zn, contributing to the persistence of antibiotic resistance by co-selection. In this study, the ileum and colon microbiome of piglets fed low (175 ppm), moderate (953 ppm), or high (2,991 ppm) concentrations of zinc oxide for 21 days after weaning were investigated using metagenomics and 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing. The pH and volatile fatty acids (VFA) were measured in cecum and colon. The colon resistome was investigated using metagenomics and PCR. The high Zn supplementation led to an increase in pH and a decrease in the VFA in both the cecum and colon. The bacterial diversity in colon was negatively impacted by the high Zn diet, with thriving Clostridiaceae and depletion of beneficial populations (e.g., Lactobacillaceae and Selenomonadaceae). Of concern, higher abundances of blaCTX-M and intI1 were observed in piglets fed with the moderate Zn diet. The findings from this study support the limitation of Zn to low concentrations.

Importance

Developing alternatives to antibiotics is imperative to mitigate the global antimicrobial resistance crisis, particularly within the livestock sector, the predominant consumer of these agents. Yet, interventions introduced without due consideration may precipitate unintended consequences. In North American swine production, supranutritional zinc supplementation in pig feed has been adopted to prevent post-weaning diarrhea and sustain profitability. However, excessive zinc disrupts iron and copper metabolism and perturbs mitochondrial homeostasis, impairing energy metabolism, antioxidant defenses, and innate immunity. Moreover, high dietary zinc increases the excretion of this heavy metal, contributing to environmental pollution and fostering antibiotic-resistant bacteria through co-selection. This study provides further evidence supporting the restriction of zinc supplementation to nutritional needs, as supranutritional diets compromised the fermentative capacity of the pig gut microbiome and increased the frequency of clinically relevant antimicrobial resistance markers.

studies.title: Supplementation of zinc-chelating peptides from <i>Holothuria scabra</i> improve zinc status in the offspring of zinc-deficient rats.
studies.abstract:
Introduction

Zinc deficiency in children remains a significant health risk, impairing their physical and cognitive maturation. Supplementation with peptide-bound zinc is thought to offer better bioavailability than inorganic zinc salts. Holothuria scabra, commonly referred to as a sea cucumber, contains peptides that may chelate zinc, potentially improving its absorption. The present study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of zinc-chelating peptides from Holothuria scabra (ZCP) supplementation in rat offspring born to zinc-deficient parental rats.

Methods

Pregnant Sprague Dawley rats were fed either a standard zinc diet (40 mg of zinc per kg of feed) or a zinc-deficient diet (4 mg of zinc per kg of feed). Twelve rat offspring born on the standard zinc diet were randomly assigned to receive either vehicle only or ZCP 40 mg/kg BW. Twenty-four offspring born from zinc-deficient maternal rats were divided into groups that received vehicle only, ZCP 4 mg/kg BW, ZCP 40 mg/kg BW, or ZnSO4 40 mg/kg BW for 3 weeks. At the end of the treatment, serum and intestinal samples were collected and analysed for zinc and metallothionein concentrations, as well as for ZIP2 and ZIP4 mRNA expressions.

Results

ZCP supplementation significantly increased serum and duodenal zinc levels, metallothionein concentration, and mRNA expressions of ZIP2/ZIP4 in zinc-deficient rat offspring compared to untreated zinc-deficient ones. Supplementation with ZCP at 4 mg/kg BW showed superior or equivalent improvements compared with ZnSO4 in most parameters.

Conclusion

Zinc chelating peptides from Holothuria scabra improved zinc plasma and duodenal concentrations by enhancing the expression of zinc transporters in zinc-deficient rat offspring. ZCP is a promising alternative to conventional inorganic zinc supplements.

studies.title: Effect of zinc on growth performance, gut morphometry, and cecal microbial community in broilers challenged with Salmonella enterica serovar typhimurium.
studies.abstract: To evaluate the effects of supplemental zinc on growth performance, gut morphometry, and the cecal microbial community in broilers challenged with Salmonella typhimurium, 180, 1-day-old male Cobb 500 broiler chicks were randomly assigned to 3 treatments with ten replicates for a 42 day experiment. The 3 treatments were: unchallenged, S. typhimurium-challenged, and S. typhimurium-challenged with 120 mg/kg of zinc supplementation in the diet. Salmonella infection caused a reduction in body-weight gain and feed intake, disrupted the intestinal structure by decreasing the villus-height/crypt-depth ratio of the ileum and increasing the apoptotic index of ileal epithelial cells. Moreover, the cecal microbial community was altered by Salmonella infection, as demonstrated by a reduced number of Lactobacillus and total bacteria. Dietary zinc supplementation improved growth performance by increasing the body-weight gain and feed intake in the challenged broilers. In addition, zinc repaired intestinal injury by reducing the apoptotic index of ileal epithelial cells, enhancing villus height and the villus-height/crypt-depth ratio of the ileum, and the proliferation index of ileal epithelial cells. Finally, zinc regulated the cecal microbial community by increasing the number of total bacteria and beneficial Lactobacillus bacteria, and reducing the number of Salmonella. The results indicated that dietary zinc supplementation improved growth performance, intestinal morphology, and intestinal microbiota in S. typhimurium-challenged broilers.

studies.title: Study on the physical, chemical, structural, and functional characteristics of quinoa peptide-zinc chelate.
studies.abstract:
Background

Zinc deficiency affects over 2 billion people worldwide, largely due to poor dietary absorption caused by inhibitors such as phytates. Conventional zinc supplements often show low bioavailability in the intestinal tract. Peptide-zinc chelates offer a promising alternative, yet quinoa-derived peptides remain underexplored as zinc carriers. This study aimed to prepare quinoa peptide-zinc chelate and characterize its physical, chemical, and functional properties.

Results

Quinoa peptides were obtained by enzymatic hydrolysis and chelated with zinc under optimized conditions. Amino acid analysis showed increased contents of glutamic acid (from 21.03 to 23.62 mg g-1), arginine (from 10.15 to 12.43 mg g-1), and lysine (from1.45 to 2.23 mg g-1) after chelation, indicating these as primary binding sites. Scanning electron microscopy and particle size analysis revealed reduced particle size (from 219.73 to 113.93 nm). Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy confirmed the involvement of H, COOH, and CO groups. Quinoa peptide-zinc chelate exhibited superior zinc solubility (95.64%) during simulated gastrointestinal digestion compared to zinc acetate (92.31%) and demonstrated significant antioxidant activity (2,2'-azino-bis(3-ethylbenzothiazoline-6-sulfonate scavenging rate: 84.53%).

Conclusion

These findings establish quinoa as a viable source of zinc-chelating peptides and support quinoa peptide-zinc chelate as a functional ingredient for enhancing zinc bioavailability. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

explanation.what_it_is_line: An essential mineral your body needs for immune function, wound healing, and protein synthesis.
explanation.what_it_is: Zinc is a metal element (Zn, atomic weight 65.4) that your body cannot make on its own — you must get it from food or supplements. It's found naturally in meat, shellfish, legumes, nuts, and seeds. In supplement form, it comes as tablets, capsules, lozenges, or powders, often bound to other compounds (like zinc gluconate or zinc picolinate) to help your body absorb it.
explanation.how_it_works_line: Activates immune cells, acts as an antioxidant, and helps enzymes build and repair proteins.
explanation.how_it_works: Zinc works in three main ways. First, it's a cofactor — a kind of molecular helper — for dozens of enzymes (protein tools) that your cells use to build and repair DNA, proteins, and other structures. Second, it directly activates immune cells (white blood cells) that fight infection and regulate inflammatory responses. Third, it acts as an antioxidant, neutralizing harmful molecules called free radicals that can damage cells. When zinc levels are adequate, your immune system can mount a faster and stronger response to threats; when zinc is low, immune function slows. It also helps maintain the lining of your gut, which is a major barrier against infection and inflammation.
explanation.safety_line: Well-tolerated in short-term studies; long-term safety and drug interactions remain largely untested.
explanation.safety_detail: Most trials reported no serious adverse events or only minor gastrointestinal symptoms (nausea, stomach upset) at standard supplementation doses. However, retrieved trials are predominantly short-term (weeks to a few months), so long-term tolerability data are limited. Zinc interacts with copper absorption and certain medications, and excess zinc can cause copper deficiency or interfere with antibiotic absorption — interactions not thoroughly explored in the provided records.
safety_bullets: Long-term supplementation safety unknown — most retrieved trials lasted weeks to months, not years.
Drug interactions untested in retrieved records: zinc may interfere with some antibiotics and reduce copper absorption if taken in excess.
Pregnant and breastfeeding women, children on fixed regimens, and people with kidney or liver disease were excluded or underrepresented in most studies — effects in these groups remain unknown.
Optimal dose and upper safety limits may vary by individual, age, and baseline zinc status — not standardized across trials.
explanation.chem_meaning: Zinc is a transition metal with a filled d-shell, making it highly reactive with proteins and enzymes — this is why it binds so tightly to cellular machinery and why even small shifts in body zinc levels can have large effects. It is not organic (no carbon backbone) and has low solubility in water alone, which is why it's formulated with organic compounds in supplements to improve absorption.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: 27 human and 4 animal studies converge on the same finding: zinc supplementation enhances immune responses and reduces infection risk or severity. Three independent meta-analyses and systematic reviews confirm this — including a 2024 review on zinc for acute respiratory infections, a 2024 systematic review on zinc for diarrhoea in children, and a 2019 review on zinc and skin immunity. RCTs show benefits in HIV infection (2025), oral lichen planus (2025), and in children with infectious diseases. At least 1,158 participants were verified across the disclosed studies, though the true total is larger.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Multiple independent systematic reviews converge on the same conclusion, and the evidence comes from adequately powered human trials. Consistency across diverse populations (children, adults, immunocompromised patients) and study designs (RCTs and meta-analyses) supports a strong grade.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: 18 human RCTs examined zinc supplementation in people with prediabetes, type 2 diabetes, and obesity. The pooled effect showed a mean reduction in blood glucose of about 10.86 mg/dL (95% confidence interval: −14.74 to −6.98). Studies ranged from 2022 to 2024 and included populations aged middle-aged to older adults. A 2023 trial in 419 people measured insulin-like growth factor and growth response; a 2023 trial in 70 people showed enhancement of antioxidant capacity alongside glucose improvement.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: The pooled effect is consistent and clinically meaningful, but only one meta-analysis exists in the provided records — replication by independent systematic reviews has not yet occurred. Human evidence is robust (18 studies, no animal studies), but single-source synthesis holds the grade at moderate rather than strong.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: 20 human and 2 animal studies show that zinc supplementation reduces inflammatory markers. Two independent meta-analyses and systematic reviews converge on this finding: a 2024 meta-analysis on primary dysmenorrhea (n=739) and a 2020 meta-analysis on acne. The pooled effect size (Hedges' g = −1.541, 95% CI: −2.268 to −0.814) indicates a large anti-inflammatory effect. RCTs in 2025–2026 demonstrated benefits in HIV infection, oral lichen planus, ADHD, and overweight adults. At least 1,127 participants were verified across disclosed studies.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Two independent meta-analyses confirm the finding across diverse inflammatory conditions, and the pooled effect is large and precise. Human RCT evidence dominates, with replication across multiple clinical populations, supporting a strong grade.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: 7 human and 5 animal studies examined zinc for gastrointestinal health and infection recovery. A 2024 systematic review on acute and persistent diarrhoea in children is the primary synthesis. RCTs include a large 2020 trial (n=2,370) on zinc and semen quality in men undergoing fertility treatment, a 2019 trial (n=52) on zinc and inflammation in treated HIV, a 2005 trial (n=28) on zinc in shigellosis, and a 2007 study on parasitic infections in children. At least 2,465 participants were verified across disclosed studies.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Only a single meta-analysis exists in the provided records, and independent replication has not occurred, which limits confidence to moderate. Human evidence is present and diverse (7 trials), but the evidence base is smaller and less robustly synthesized than for immune function or inflammation.

explanation.evidence_base: The evidence is predominantly human (52 of 63 studies), with RCTs and meta-analyses dominating. Studies span 2005–2026, with most published 2019 or later, indicating active current research. Three meta-analyses independently confirm immune function and inflammation outcomes; blood sugar and gut outcomes rest on single systematic reviews, which limits replication. Across outcomes, sample sizes in disclosed abstracts total over 1,000 verified participants, though most abstracts omit sizes, suggesting the true total is substantially larger.
explanation.open_questions: The provided records show strong coverage in children and adults with common infections or metabolic disorders, but notably sparse representation of pregnant women, adolescents, people with severe kidney disease, and the elderly — whether zinc works as well in these groups is unknown from the studies shown. Trial durations are predominantly short (weeks to a few months); long-term effects (beyond 6 months) are underrepresented, and no records address sustained supplementation safety. Gut and digestion outcomes rest on fewer studies than immune function, leaving uncertainty about dose optimization and which digestive conditions benefit most.

appraisal.headline: Zinc shows consistent evidence for immune function and inflammation, but heterogeneous populations, inconsistent dosing/formulation reporting, and lack of independent replication for blood sugar and gut outcomes limit confidence in those latter claims.

concerns.issue: Blood sugar outcome lacks independent replication
concerns.detail: The blood sugar grade (Moderate) rests on a single 2022 meta-analysis (n=265), with no independently-conducted systematic review to verify the conclusion. In contrast, immune function and inflammation each show 2–3 independent meta-analyses. A pooled effect of mean_diff -10.86 mg/dL appears precise, but replicability in the meta-analytic synthesis is undemonstrated, making this outcome vulnerable to selective reporting or methodological choices within that single analysis.

concerns.issue: Gut/digestion evidence is sparse and unmeta-replicated
concerns.detail: Only 12 studies total (7 human, 5 animal), with a single systematic review that has not been independently replicated. Four studies report sample sizes (n: 15, 28, 52, 2370), but the median is inflated by one outlier; 8 of 12 studies do not report n at all. Without a second independent meta-analysis, and given heterogeneity in outcomes (diarrhea, parasitic infection, HPV clearance, HIV markers), the 'Moderate' grade overstates confidence in a coherent effect.

concerns.issue: Majority of studies omit sample size in abstracts
concerns.detail: Across immune function (31 studies: 11 report n), inflammation (22 studies: 9 report n), and blood sugar (18 studies: 11 report n), 50–65% of abstracts do not disclose sample size. This prevents assessment of whether small studies cluster in one direction and large trials in another—a common pattern in supplementation research—and obscures whether the true total evidence base is robust or dominated by many small, underpowered trials.

concerns.issue: Heterogeneity in populations obscures clinical specificity
concerns.detail: The immune function studies span atopic dermatitis, acute diarrhea in children, oral lichen planus, HIV infection, obesity, HPV clearance, and pre-schooler immune markers. The inflammation outcome includes dysmenorrhea, acne, ADHD, Behçet's disease, and neonatal respiratory distress. No study records report which populations show the largest effects or whether zinc is genuinely effective across this range or only in a subset. The pooled hedges_g -1.541 for inflammation is a large effect, but without subgroup analysis visible, it is unclear whether this reflects true uniformity or selective reporting of positive trials in heterogeneous conditions.

concerns.issue: Dosing, formulation, and duration not synthesized in records
concerns.detail: Study records include trials of zinc sulfate, zinc gluconate, chelated zinc peptides, and unspecified 'zinc supplementation,' spanning durations from brief interventions to chronic supplementation. No records report whether meta-analyses stratified by dose, chemical form, or duration, or whether these variables confound the pooled effects. Variation in formulation is particularly relevant because bioavailability differs markedly (e.g., zinc sulfate vs. oxide), yet this is invisible in the abstracted grades.

appraisal.mechanism_check: Zinc is a known cofactor for immune cell function (T-cell activation, NK cell killing, neutrophil chemotaxis) and is involved in redox regulation and NF-κB signaling, which plausibly supports the immune function and inflammation outcomes. However, the clinical leap from in vitro mechanistic studies to broad population-level efficacy in heterogeneous conditions (acne, dysmenorrhea, HIV-associated inflammation, ADHD) is large. For blood sugar, the proposed mechanism (enhanced antioxidant response, IGF-1/IGFBP-3 modulation) is biologically plausible but more indirect; the records show no mechanistic validation that this pathway actually drives the observed -10.86 mg/dL glucose reduction in the meta-analysis.
appraisal.strongest_counterargument: A skeptic would observe that the evidence base is dominated by small, heterogeneous RCTs in diverse populations with incomplete reporting of sample sizes and methodology, and that the pooled effects—especially for inflammation (hedges_g -1.541) and blood sugar (−10.86 mg/dL)—are implausibly large for a micronutrient in otherwise adequately-nourished populations. They would note that the blood sugar and gut outcomes each rely on a single meta-analysis without independent replication, and that selective reporting of positive trials in high-impact journals could inflate the apparent effect size. Finally, they would argue that without stratified analysis by dose, formulation, and population subgroup, the grades conflate 'zinc works somewhere, in some form, at some dose' with genuine clinical utility.
appraisal.what_would_change_the_picture: Independent replication of the blood sugar and gut/digestion meta-analyses by separate research groups using pre-specified protocols; large (n ≥ 200) pragmatic RCTs reporting zinc dose, formulation, serum zinc levels at baseline and endpoint, and stratified subgroup effects by age, nutritional status, and disease etiology; and explicit accounting for studies that tested zinc in isolation versus combined micronutrient formulations.

explanation_es.what_it_is_line: Un mineral esencial que tu cuerpo necesita para la función inmunológica, cicatrización de heridas y síntesis de proteínas.
explanation_es.what_it_is: El zinc es un elemento metálico (Zn, peso atómico 65.4) que tu cuerpo no puede producir por sí solo — debes obtenerlo de alimentos o suplementos. Se encuentra naturalmente en carne, mariscos, legumbres, nueces y semillas. En forma de suplemento, viene como tabletas, cápsulas, pastillas o polvos, a menudo unidos a otros compuestos (como gluconato de zinc o picolinato de zinc) para ayudar a tu cuerpo a absorberlo.
explanation_es.how_it_works_line: Activa células inmunológicas, actúa como antioxidante y ayuda a las enzimas a construir y reparar proteínas.
explanation_es.how_it_works: El zinc funciona de tres formas principales. Primero, es un cofactor — una especie de ayudante molecular — para docenas de enzimas (herramientas proteicas) que tus células usan para construir y reparar ADN, proteínas y otras estructuras. Segundo, activa directamente células inmunológicas (glóbulos blancos) que combaten infecciones y regulan respuestas inflamatorias. Tercero, actúa como antioxidante, neutralizando moléculas dañinas llamadas radicales libres que pueden dañar las células. Cuando los niveles de zinc son adecuados, tu sistema inmunológico puede montar una respuesta más rápida y fuerte a las amenazas; cuando el zinc es bajo, la función inmunológica se ralentiza. También ayuda a mantener el revestimiento de tu intestino, que es una barrera importante contra infecciones e inflamación.
explanation_es.safety_line: Bien tolerado en estudios a corto plazo; la seguridad a largo plazo e interacciones medicamentosas siguen siendo en gran medida no probadas.
explanation_es.safety_detail: La mayoría de los ensayos no reportaron eventos adversos graves o solo síntomas gastrointestinales menores (náuseas, malestar estomacal) a dosis estándar de suplementación. Sin embargo, los ensayos recuperados son predominantemente a corto plazo (semanas a pocos meses), por lo que los datos de tolerabilidad a largo plazo son limitados. El zinc interactúa con la absorción de cobre y ciertos medicamentos, y el exceso de zinc puede causar deficiencia de cobre o interferir con la absorción de antibióticos — interacciones no exploradas a fondo en los registros proporcionados.
safety_bullets: Seguridad de la suplementación a largo plazo desconocida — la mayoría de los ensayos recuperados duraron semanas a meses, no años.
Interacciones medicamentosas no probadas en los registros recuperados: el zinc puede interferir con algunos antibióticos y reducir la absorción de cobre si se toma en exceso.

Mujeres embarazadas y lactantes, niños con regímenes fijos y personas con enfermedad renal o hepática fueron excluidas o subrepresentadas en la mayoría de los estudios — los efectos en estos grupos siguen siendo desconocidos.
La dosis óptima y los límites de seguridad superior pueden variar según el individuo, edad y estado basal de zinc — no están estandarizados entre ensayos.
explanation_es.chem_meaning: El zinc es un metal de transición con una capa d completa, lo que lo hace altamente reactivo con proteínas y enzimas — esta es la razón por la que se une tan firmemente a la maquinaria celular y por qué incluso cambios pequeños en los niveles de zinc corporal pueden tener grandes efectos. No es orgánico (sin esqueleto de carbono) y tiene baja solubilidad en agua sola, razón por la cual se formula con compuestos orgánicos en suplementos para mejorar la absorción.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: 27 estudios humanos y 4 estudios en animales convergen en el mismo hallazgo: la suplementación con zinc mejora las respuestas inmunológicas y reduce el riesgo o la gravedad de la infección. Tres metanálisis independientes y revisiones sistemáticas confirman esto — incluyendo una revisión de 2024 sobre zinc para infecciones respiratorias agudas, una revisión sistemática de 2024 sobre zinc para diarrea en niños y una revisión de 2019 sobre zinc e inmunidad de la piel. Los ensayos controlados aleatorios muestran beneficios en infección por VIH (2025), liquen plano oral (2025) y en niños con enfermedades infecciosas. Al menos 1,158 participantes fueron verificados en los estudios divulgados, aunque el total verdadero es mayor.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Múltiples revisiones sistemáticas independientes convergen en la misma conclusión, y la evidencia proviene de ensayos humanos adecuadamente potenciados. La consistencia entre poblaciones diversas (niños, adultos, pacientes inmunocomprometidos) y diseños de estudios (ensayos controlados aleatorios y metanálisis) apoya una calificación fuerte.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: 18 ensayos controlados aleatorios humanos examinaron suplementación con zinc en personas con prediabetes, diabetes tipo 2 y obesidad. El efecto combinado mostró una reducción media de glucosa en sangre de aproximadamente 10.86 mg/dL (intervalo de confianza 95%: −14.74 a −6.98). Los estudios oscilaron entre 2022 y 2024 e incluyeron poblaciones de adultos de mediana edad a adultos mayores. Un ensayo de 2023 en 419 personas midió el factor de crecimiento similar a la insulina y la respuesta de crecimiento; un ensayo de 2023 en 70 personas mostró mejora de la capacidad antioxidante junto con mejora de la glucosa.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: El efecto combinado es consistente y clínicamente significativo, pero solo existe un metanálisis en los registros proporcionados — la replicación por revisiones sistemáticas independientes aún no ha ocurrido. La evidencia humana es robusta (18 estudios, sin estudios en animales), pero la síntesis de fuente única mantiene la calificación en moderada en lugar de fuerte.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: 20 estudios humanos y 2 estudios en animales muestran que la suplementación con zinc reduce marcadores inflamatorios. Dos metanálisis independientes y revisiones sistemáticas convergen en este hallazgo: un metanálisis de 2024 sobre dismenorrea primaria (n=739) y un metanálisis de 2020 sobre acné. El tamaño del efecto combinado (g de Hedges = −1.541, intervalo de confianza 95%: −2.268 a −0.814) indica un gran efecto antiinflamatorio. Los ensayos controlados aleatorios de 2025–2026 demostraron beneficios en infección por VIH, liquen plano oral, TDAH y adultos con sobrepeso. Al menos 1,127 participantes fueron verificados entre los estudios divulgados.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Dos metanálisis independientes confirman el hallazgo en diversas condiciones inflamatorias, y el efecto combinado es grande y preciso. La evidencia de ensayos controlados aleatorios humanos domina, con replicación entre múltiples poblaciones clínicas, lo que apoya una calificación fuerte.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: 7 estudios humanos y 5 estudios en animales examinaron zinc para la salud gastrointestinal y la recuperación de infecciones. Una revisión sistemática de 2024 sobre diarrea aguda y persistente en niños es la síntesis primaria. Los ensayos controlados aleatorios incluyen un gran ensayo de 2020 (n=2,370) sobre zinc y calidad del semen en hombres sometidos a tratamiento de fertilidad, un ensayo de 2019 (n=52) sobre zinc e inflamación en VIH tratado, un ensayo de 2005 (n=28) sobre zinc en shigelosis y un estudio de 2007 sobre infecciones parasitarias en niños. Al menos 2,465 participantes fueron verificados entre los estudios divulgados.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Solo existe un metanálisis en los registros proporcionados, y la replicación independiente no ha ocurrido, lo que limita la confianza a moderada. La evidencia humana está presente y es diversa (7 ensayos), pero la base de evidencia es más pequeña y menos robustamente sintetizada que para función inmunológica o inflamación.

explanation_es.evidence_base: La evidencia es predominantemente humana (52 de 63 estudios), con ensayos controlados aleatorios y metanálisis dominando. Los estudios abarcan 2005–2026, con la mayoría publicados en 2019 o después, lo que indica investigación actual activa. Tres metanálisis confirman independientemente resultados de función inmunológica e inflamación; los resultados de azúcar en sangre e intestino descansan en revisiones sistemáticas únicas, lo que limita la replicación. Entre los resultados, los tamaños de muestra en resúmenes divulgados totalizan más de 1,000 participantes verificados, aunque la mayoría de los resúmenes omiten tamaños, sugiriendo que el total verdadero es sustancialmente mayor.
explanation_es.open_questions: Los registros proporcionados muestran cobertura fuerte en niños y adultos con infecciones comunes o trastornos metabólicos, pero notablemente escasa representación de mujeres embarazadas, adolescentes, personas con enfermedad renal grave y adultos mayores — si el zinc funciona igual de bien en estos grupos es desconocido de los estudios mostrados. Las duraciones de los ensayos son predominantemente cortas (semanas a pocos meses); los efectos a largo plazo (más allá de 6 meses) están subrepresentados, y ningún registro aborda la seguridad de la suplementación sostenida. Los resultados de intestino y digestión descansan en menos estudios que la función inmunológica, dejando incertidumbre sobre la optimización de dosis y qué condiciones digestivas se benefician más.

appraisal_es.headline: Zinc muestra evidencia consistente para la función inmunológica e inflamación, pero poblaciones heterogéneas, reportes inconsistentes de dosis/formulación y falta de replicación independiente para resultados de glucosa en sangre y salud intestinal limitan la confianza en estas últimas afirmaciones.

concerns.issue: El resultado de glucosa en sangre carece de replicación independiente
concerns.detail: La calificación de glucosa en sangre (Moderada) se basa en un único metanálisis de 2022 (n=265), sin revisión sistemática independiente que verifique la conclusión. En contraste, la función inmunológica e inflamación muestran cada una 2–3 metanálisis independientes. Un efecto agrupado de media_diff -10.86 mg/dL parece preciso, pero la replicabilidad en la síntesis del metanálisis no está demostrada, lo que hace que este resultado sea vulnerable a sesgo de reporte selectivo o decisiones metodológicas dentro de ese único análisis.

concerns.issue: La evidencia de salud intestinal/digestión es escasa y no replicada mediante metanálisis
concerns.detail: Solo 12 estudios totales (7 humanos, 5 animales), con una única revisión sistemática que no ha sido replicada independientemente. Cuatro estudios reportan tamaños de muestra (n: 15, 28, 52, 2370), pero la mediana está inflada por un valor atípico; 8 de 12 estudios no reportan n en absoluto. Sin un segundo metanálisis independiente, y dada la heterogeneidad en los resultados (diarrea, infección parasitaria, aclaramiento de VPH, marcadores de VIH), la calificación 'Moderada' sobrestima la confianza en un efecto coherente.

concerns.issue: La mayoría de los estudios omiten el tamaño de la muestra en los resúmenes
concerns.detail: En función inmunológica (31 estudios: 11 reportan n), inflamación (22 estudios: 9 reportan n) y glucosa en sangre (18 estudios: 11 reportan n), el 50–65% de los resúmenes no revelan el tamaño de la muestra. Esto impide evaluar si los estudios pequeños se agrupan en una dirección y los ensayos grandes en otra—un patrón común en la investigación de suplementos—y oscurece si la verdadera base de evidencia total es robusta o está dominada por muchos ensayos pequeños sin potencia suficiente.

concerns.issue: La heterogeneidad en poblaciones oscurece la especificidad clínica
concerns.detail: Los estudios de función inmunológica abarcan dermatitis atópica, diarrea aguda en niños, liquen plano oral, infección por VIH, obesidad, aclaramiento de VPH y marcadores inmunológicos en preescolares. El resultado de inflamación incluye dismenorrea, acné, TDAH, enfermedad de Behçet y síndrome de dificultad respiratoria neonatal. Ningún registro de estudio reporta qué poblaciones muestran los mayores efectos o si el zinc es genuinamente efectivo en este rango o solo en un subconjunto. El hedges_g agrupado -1.541 para inflamación es un efecto grande, pero sin análisis de subgrupos visible, no está claro si esto refleja una uniformidad verdadera o reporte selectivo de ensayos positivos en condiciones heterogéneas.

concerns.issue: La dosis, formulación y duración no se sintetizaron en los registros
concerns.detail: Los registros de estudios incluyen ensayos de sulfato de zinc, gluconato de zinc, péptidos quelados de zinc y 'suplementación de zinc' no especificada, abarcando duraciones desde intervenciones breves hasta suplementación crónica. Ningún registro reporta si los metanálisis estratificaron por dosis, forma química o duración, o si estas variables confunden los efectos agrupados. La variación en formulación es particularmente relevante porque la biodisponibilidad difiere notablemente (p. ej., sulfato de zinc vs. óxido), pero esto es invisible en las calificaciones extraídas.

appraisal_es.mechanism_check: Zinc es un cofactor conocido para la función de células inmunológicas (activación de células T, actividad citotóxica de células NK, quimiotaxis de neutrófilos) e interviene en la regulación redox y la señalización de NF-κB, lo que respalda plausiblemente los resultados de función inmunológica e inflamación. Sin embargo, el salto clínico de estudios mecanísticos in vitro a la eficacia amplia a nivel poblacional en condiciones heterogéneas (acné, dismenorrea, inflamación asociada al VIH, TDAH) es grande. Para la glucosa en sangre, el mecanismo propuesto (respuesta antioxidante mejorada, modulación de IGF-1/IGFBP-3) es biológicamente plausible pero más indirecto; los registros no muestran validación mecanística de que esta vía realmente impulse la reducción de glucosa de -10.86 mg/dL observada en el metanálisis.
appraisal_es.strongest_counterargument: Un escéptico observaría que la base de evidencia está dominada por pequeños ensayos controlados aleatorizados heterogéneos en poblaciones diversas con reporte incompleto de tamaños de muestra y metodología, y que los efectos agrupados—especialmente para inflamación (hedges_g -1.541) y glucosa en sangre (−10.86 mg/dL)—son implausiblemente grandes para un micronutriente en poblaciones adecuadamente nutridas. Señalaría que los resultados de glucosa en sangre y salud intestinal se basan cada uno en un único metanálisis sin replicación independiente, y que el reporte selectivo de ensayos positivos en revistas de alto impacto podría inflar el tamaño del efecto aparente. Finalmente, argumentaría que sin análisis estratificado por dosis, formulación y subgrupo poblacional, las calificaciones confunden 'zinc funciona en algún lugar, en alguna forma, a alguna dosis' con utilidad clínica genuina.
appraisal_es.what_would_change_the_picture: Replicación independiente de los metanálisis de glucosa en sangre y salud intestinal/digestión por grupos de investigación separados utilizando protocolos preespecificados; ensayos controlados aleatorizados pragmáticos grandes (n ≥ 200) que reportan dosis de zinc, formulación, niveles de zinc sérico al inicio y punto final, y efectos de subgrupos estratificados por edad, estado nutricional y etiología de la enfermedad; y contabilización explícita de estudios que probaron zinc en aislamiento versus formulaciones de micronutrientes combinados.
